questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Primarily that Macquarie University is located in Sydney since I like the combination of nature and city. Also Macquarie has a lot of interesting courses to offer for international law students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. I didn't attend orientation week due to a cancelled flight, but both the course convenor and the staff at Macquarie were helpful and kind.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I didn't attend orientation week, most assistance and information were given online via mail which worked out fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. However, rent was quite expensive. We paid 2600 per week for a 4 bedroom house in Bondi Junction. Less expensive housing is possible to find, but it is also my impression that there is a bigger demand as such.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
The commute can be quite long if you don't have a car. The commute from Bondi Junction to Macquarie was approx. 1,5-2 hours each way with train. The car ride was 30-40 minutes without traffic and 1 hour in rush hours. 
Riding the train is however fairly inexpensive costing approx. 5-6 AUD each way from Macquarie to Bondi Junction. 
Parking at campus is easy with plenty of space and cost 12 AUD for the whole day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite expensive for what you get.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Relatively easy and quick response from the staff.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Macquarie had a great catalog of courses available.
Some law courses required pre-requisite waivers which was processed often within a day. When waiver was received it was easy to register for the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online tutorials and mailing with the staff.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got accepted into all of the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of what pre-requisites you need to attend the courses and apply for a waiver.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some courses was fairly easy and others quite tough. The curriculum was varied a lot with some courses having 20-50 pages of reading per week and others 150-200 per week. The average study load for my courses was approx. 400-600 pages a week which was quite overwhelming to begin with. However, I quickly chose not to follow all of the readings and instead focus on select courses and attending tutorials and lectures.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Please read the answer above.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar. At Macquarie students were also encouraged to participate and ask questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Law, Law of the Sea, International Trade Law, Climate Change Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Law and International Law of the Sea. These courses had a reasonable study load and the instructors were very kind, skilled and helpful especially in Law of the Sea.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
We bought a car which came with a lot of unexpected costs such as registration, insurance, road tolls, parking permits etc. 
Other than that we had to pay for pool service, lawn mowing and other costs related to our house.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive. Sydney is a quite expensive city. However, traveling domestically in Australia by flight is fairly inexpensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very nice facilities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nice athletic facilities. Also very nice with the green areas surrounding campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The green areas surrounding campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around Australia and go to the beaches.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Australians are easygoing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nightlife closes early. Often around 12 or 1. You can't make noise or have social gatherings outside after 11.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor living with going to beaches. Also Australians are very kind and open.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the study loads in some of the courses. Also consider where you live in Sydney since the commute can be quite long.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Personal and academic development. Also I got a lot of good experiences and memories.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to the study load at first since it was quite overwhelming.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
